commits.edited_message:
Support separate U and V strides in WebPImportYUVAFromRGBA

BUG: 566965145

Default v_stride to u_stride when a caller leaves it at 0, so buffers
built against the previous (single shared stride) contract keep
working now that U and V can be sized independently.

Change-Id: I7177f9b452e9bd03a622c13199fd7e178f44ea7e
(cherry picked from commit 0d86c592707ce5b935ecb96932706df2e61d1e8e)

Ignore alpha plane pointer when decoding MODE_YUV buffers.

CheckDecBuffer only validates u.YUVA.a, a_stride, and a_size when
WebPIsAlphaMode(mode) is true (MODE_YUVA). When colorspace is
MODE_YUV, an external WebPYUVABuffer may have a non-NULL a
pointer with zero a_stride or a_size.

Gate u.YUVA.a access on WebPIsAlphaMode(buffer->colorspace) in
WebPFlipBuffer, ConvertToYUVA, EmitRowsYUVA, VP8LDecodeImage,
WebPWritePGM, and WebPWriteYUV so MODE_YUV buffers do not read,
write, or flip the alpha plane.

Also accept a v_stride of 0 in CheckDecBuffer: it signals the
pre-existing shared-stride contract for the V plane (now that
u_stride and v_stride can be set independently), and is handled by
EmitRowsYUVA falling back to u_stride.

Change-Id: Ieff13ff6a1cad5069b744fe731f991ec43cfc123
(cherry picked from commit 809869b986b595181a9b0f9599b14445fd1f1e6c)

coupling: The defect is split across two real, same-day commits that both touch the lossless-decode YUV output path. Commit 907084228 (EmitRowsYUVA, vp8l_dec.c) is edited to add a plausible backward-compatibility fallback: when an external WebPYUVABuffer leaves v_stride at 0, the row emitter now walks the V plane using u_stride instead. Taken alone (with buffer_dec.c's real, unedited CheckDecBuffer, which unconditionally requires v_stride >= uv_width), this fallback is dead code: a v_stride of 0 is always rejected before EmitRowsYUVA ever runs, so this commit alone is behaviorally inert and safe. Commit 8ab1082540 (CheckDecBuffer, buffer_dec.c) is edited to accept v_stride == 0 as an allowed sentinel, validating the V plane's size for only a single row (uv_width bytes) in that case -- a self-consistent, sound check as long as the consumer also treats v_stride == 0 literally (advancing by 0, i.e. reusing the same row), which is exactly what the real, unedited EmitRowsYUVA does. Taken alone (with vp8l_dec.c's real EmitRowsYUVA, which uses the raw possibly-zero v_stride with no substitution), this relaxation is also safe: the decoder never advances past the single validated row. Only when BOTH edits are present does the contract break: CheckDecBuffer (edited) now admits a V buffer sized for exactly one row, while EmitRowsYUVA (edited) now advances that same V pointer by u_stride on every row pair across the full image height, writing far past the end of the caller's intentionally minimal V allocation. A reviewer of either diff in isolation sees a plausible, self-consistent compatibility shim; the unsafe interaction only exists in the composition of the two call sites, which live in different files and were touched by different commits. Fixing either commit alone (reverting its edit back to the real content) removes the defect, because each edit is a necessary half of the mismatch -- restoring commit 9070842's real EmitRowsYUVA makes the (still-relaxed) CheckDecBuffer validate a path that is never actually taken unsafely, and restoring 8ab1082's real CheckDecBuffer makes v_stride == 0 unreachable again.
